in: Option list container surface — Primary + Secondary contexts (background/primary, background/secondary).
Option-row backgrounds — per-context (Primary/Secondary) × per-state (Default/Hover/Selected). Default at-rest aliases container surface (surface-on-surface).
Option text — default + selected (selected ships value-coincident with default; future-lever).
Field trailing disclosure icon — single token covering both Open states; shape swaps, colour does not.
Per-option tick icon on Selected variants.
Per-option bottom-border divider (stroke on each item-row root).
Disabled option row opacity — the row dims by opacity with all colour bindings left at their default values. Option row only; the field's own disabled treatment comes from component/-input.
out: Filter/multiselect clear icon (the inline 'x' that empties the current filter text or selection) — MOVED to component/-input 2026-08-06 as icon/control-default + icon/control-hover. The affordance lives in the shared Input/Slot/Suffix helper as a boolean, hidden by default, so the tokens belong to the input family rather than to Dropdown. Renamed from 'clear' to 'control' because under -input the token describes the interactive icon in a slot — the role — matching prefix/suffix/error, rather than one affordance. Dropdown is simply its first consumer.

Per-option Nested-type chevron (the `>` on Type=Nested item rows) — REMOVED 2026-08-06. Type=Nested is inherited from the Tegel UI Library and has no counterpart in either codebase: no optgroup, submenu or grouping mechanism in Scania core or tegel-lite, and the option's only slot is label text. The affordance uses regular suffix-icon treatment rather than a dedicated variable. Variant parked on canvas, selectable per item row.
Multi-select pill rendering in field — Scania core (dropdown.tsx) renders comma-separated labels, not pills; tegel-lite same. No chip-style tokens needed.

_divergence.option-mode-variant-dropped: APPLIED to this spec 2026-08-08, NOT YET PUSHED. The option set's Mode Variant axis was removed on canvas (60 variants to 30) because both codebases show it redundant, and the mode treatment moves to the list container, where it pairs with the top-level Dropdown set. EVIDENCE: Scania core paints the list via --tds-dropdown-bg and the option via --tds-dropdown-option-background with byte-identical values in all four combinations — Light primary grey-50/grey-50, Light secondary white/white, Dark primary grey-900/grey-900, Dark secondary grey-850/grey-850 — so the option's mode background repainted exactly what the container already painted. tegel-lite had already reached the same place: --dropdown-option-background is defined in _tl-dropdown-vars.scss and never consumed anywhere in the package, so its options are transparent at rest and the list paints. Neither brand mode-splits the interactive states either: core's --tds-dropdown-option-background-selected is one value per theme rather than per mode variant, and core's hover sets no background at all. CONSEQUENCE: three tokens removed — background/item/secondary/{default,hover,selected-default} — and three renamed to drop a qualifier with no sibling left to distinguish from: background/item/primary/{default,hover,selected-default} became background/item/{default,hover,selected-default}. Spec 13 to 10. WHAT THE REMOVED TOKENS CARRIED, so it is recoverable rather than merely gone: secondary/default aliased background/secondary in all four modes and was never bound to anything; secondary/hover was traton/color/grey/150 Light, color/background/layer-03 Dark, scania/color/grey/100 Scania-Light, color/background/layer-03 Scania-Dark; secondary/selected-default was color/background/layer-02 in both TRATON modes, scania/color/grey/150 Scania-Light, scania/color/grey/750 Scania-Dark. The only thing genuinely lost is one step of primary-versus-secondary contrast on dark selected rows, which the Tegel UI Library does draw (grey/800 versus grey/750) but neither codebase implements. FIGMA STILL HOLDS THE OLD SHAPE: all 13 variables are live on branch BRANCH:dropdown-11a under their old names. Reconciling needs a push — three deletes, which must clear the Scania child-collection overrides first via removeOverrideForMode or the overrides strand, plus three renames that preserve variable IDs. variables.name: component/dropdown/background/primary
variables.comment: Option list container — Primary surface. Leaf-level per Popover precedent (component/popover/background/primary).

variables.name: component/dropdown/background/item/default
variables.comment: Item at rest — invisible, so the List container's surface shows through. The row carries no colour of its own; the primary/secondary treatment lives on the List, which is why the option set no longer needs a Mode Variant axis. This is how tegel-lite already ships it: --dropdown-option-background is defined in _tl-dropdown-vars.scss and never consumed anywhere in the package, so its rows are transparent and the list paints. The token is kept rather than dropped so the row still has a named at-rest state to sit beside hover and selected-default, and so a future decision to give rows their own surface has somewhere to land. DELIBERATE DEPARTURE from convention-surface-on-surface, which says an at-rest surface should alias its container rather than background/none: that rule assumes the child knows which container it is on, and after the Mode Variant drop this one does not. Resolved 2026-08-10 by Max; an earlier pass wrongly left it aliasing background/primary, which would have painted Primary's colour on a Secondary list.

variables.name: component/dropdown/background/item/hover
variables.comment: Rename from existing component/dropdown/hover (VariableID:14121:114024). Light primitives unwrap INTERNAL/surface/100 indirection. VERIFIED live via Variables panel UI (2026-06): Scania-Light renders #EDEFF3, confirmed = scania/color/grey/100 (REST hex search against the Primitive collection, single exact match). DARK MODES REPOINTED 2026-08-25: both were color/background/layer-02, which is also what background/secondary resolves to — so on a Secondary list the hover step was invisible in both brands (TRATON #002429 on #002429, Scania #1C222B on #1C222B). Reported from the dev side, confirmed via the REST brand-mode path. TRATON now layer-03 (#003137); Scania cannot use layer-03 because in Scania it resolves to grey/800, which background/item/selected-default already owns, so Scania takes grey/750 (#2D3643) — clear of layer-01 #15181D, layer-02 #1C222B and selected #242C37. MIXED ALIAS STRATEGY IS DELIBERATE: Light aliases brand primitives because layer-03 in Light is #F6F3E9, identical to layer-01, so a semantic alias there would collide with the Primary surface. Do not harmonise. ONE TOKEN, NOT SPLIT PER VARIANT: QA proposed primary-hover/secondary-hover, but Dropdown/List/Option has no Mode variant property (its axes are Size x Type x State x Selected) — the axis lives on Dropdown/List, so a per-variant token would have nothing to bind against on the row that carries the fill. Cost of the single value is a two-step hover jump on Primary lists, accepted — 2 steps in TRATON (blue/950 to blue/850), 3 in Scania (grey/900 to grey/750, because grey/800 is occupied by selected-default), so the brands are not symmetric in step count. RENDER-VERIFIED 2026-08-25 on branch BRANCH:dropdown-hover-repoint, Mode variant=Secondary + Size=Medium open, in BOTH brands at Dark: TRATON hover reads clearly lighter than the layer-02 surface it sits on, and Scania's three rows separate as Default grey/850 < Selected grey/800 < Hover grey/750 with the hierarchy running hover-above-selected. Max confirmed the Scania gap (#2D3643 vs #242C37, the tightest pair in the set) reads adequately on canvas; confidence raised Proposed to Confirmed on that basis. NOTE the direction differs by brand: Scania's selected sits lighter than its list surface, TRATON's sits darker (selected-default aliases layer-01 regardless of container). That asymmetry is the selected treatment Max and Flavio already ruled intentional, not a defect of this change.

variables.name: component/dropdown/background/item/selected-default
variables.comment: Option row at Selected on the Primary container. Scania values taken from the Tegel UI Library (Scania canvas source of truth, file d8bTgEx7h694MSesi2CTLF, Dropdown/List Item 33822:144518), read 2026-08-06: Mode=Light bound to grey/150 (#E0E5EB), Mode=Dark Primary bound to grey/800 (#242C37). Confirmed by direct fill-binding probe, not inferred. Scania core code independently agrees on Light (--tds-dropdown-option-background-selected: --tds-grey-150). TRATON values keep the container surface, so the selected row carries no background distinction in TRATON today — the tick is the only marker. RENAMED from the existing variable component/dropdown/focus (VariableID:14121:114023) rather than created new — the variable ID and its history are preserved. That variable was misnamed: it painted a canvas Focus variant while its bridge property drove tegel-lite's SELECTED option background. Renaming puts the name where the behaviour already was. The old CSS custom property name disappears; whether code keeps an alias for contract reasons is the consumers' call, not this cluster's. The INTERNAL surface/300 placeholder currently bound on the Selected=True nodes is NOT promoted — those 8 nodes rebind to this token.

variables.name: component/dropdown/text/item/default
variables.comment: Option text at rest. Canvas-confirmed across all probed variants (Default + Hover + Selected text all bind to color/text/strong).

variables.name: component/dropdown/text/item/selected-default
variables.comment: Option text when Selected. Value-coincident with default today; ships as separate token to reserve future lever (e.g. selected emphasis treatment).

variables.name: component/dropdown/icon/default
variables.comment: Field trailing disclosure icon. Named bare per the Accordion precedent (component/accordion/icon/default, also a chevron) and convention-icon-role-not-glyph — the descriptor carries the role, never the glyph. Unambiguous because the option-row icons are scoped under item/. Open=False renders icon/shared/chevron_down, Open=True renders chevron_up; colour is identical across both, so one token covers the shape swap (canvas-confirmed). Rides Text Field's existing suffix icon slot as an instance swap; the colour override exists because -input/icon/suffix-default resolves to a text semantic while this needs an icon one.

variables.name: component/dropdown/icon/item/selected-default
variables.comment: Single-select tick on Selected variants. Inner VECTORs (Traton + Scania) bound to color/icon/strong today. Outer INSTANCE has raw #ffffff fill — pre-existing canvas drift (see _divergence).

variables.name: component/dropdown/border/item/divider-default
variables.comment: Per-option bottom-border. Lives on each item-row's root stroke (canvas-confirmed: variant root stroke bound to color/border/discrete directly today).

variables.name: component/dropdown/opacity/disabled
variables.comment: Disabled option row. Applied as opacity on the row with every colour binding left at its State=Default value, per Max's rule 2026-08-08 that any disabled state binds the default values and then applies an opacity token. Shape matches the ten components already shipping component/{slug}/opacity/disabled — FLOAT, brand-namespaced primitive aliases, explicit per-brand bindings. DELIBERATE DEPARTURE from both codebases, which currently express a disabled option with a distinct foreground colour rather than opacity; opacity is the system-wide format going forward and code adopting it is a dev-side follow-up, not a blocker. Two things make it safe here specifically: the row is transparent at rest, so the opacity only touches the label and the tick or checkbox; and disabled implies closed, so a disabled wrapper never renders rows and two opacities cannot compound. The nested Checkbox on multiselect rows stays on its default treatment rather than being set disabled, so component/checkbox/opacity/disabled never stacks on top. Accepted trade-off: a colour chooses the disabled result while opacity computes it, so the same value lands differently over a Secondary list than a Primary one — not a blocker, since disabled text is exempt from WCAG contrast minimums. Applies to the option row only; the wrapper's own disabled treatment comes from component/-input/opacity/disabled through the nested field, canvas-verified 2026-08-12 (wrapper opacity 1, Trigger 1, Text Field 0.25 — no compounding).

variables.name: component/dropdown/border/radius-default
variables.comment: Option list container corner radius, all four corners. Added 2026-08-12 (Max's direction) to replace an INTERNAL alias found on canvas at close-out: Dropdown/List bound INTERNAL/border__wip/UNSORTED/medium on all four corners, which the never-alias-to-INTERNAL policy forbids shipping. Value derived from the closest analogue rather than chosen — Popover is the same thing, a floating container surface, and ships traton/unit/4 with scania/unit/4; -input, block, message, toast and segmented-control agree, and the List already rendered at literal 4, so this is a like-for-like replacement with no visual change. Flat border/radius-default form per convention-border-radius-naming; the nested border/radius/default seen on badge, button and chip is legacy. Only one radius token: nothing in Dropdown needs a none or full variant. The option rows deliberately carry no radius token and sit at literal 0 — they are inside elements within the list with no overflow treatment, so square corners and a square -focus/ring/radius/none helper are correct by design rather than an omission (Max, 2026-08-12). This token covers the container only; the Trigger's radius comes from component/-input/border/radius-*.

_openQuestions.non-colour-bindings-unswept: OPEN, logged 2026-08-12. Every binding sweep run during this cluster examined fills, strokes and opacity only. Radius, spacing, padding, sizing and effects were never checked on any of the four Dropdown sets. That gap hid a real policy breach until the very end: Dropdown/List bound INTERNAL/border__wip/UNSORTED/medium on all four corners, which the never-alias-to-INTERNAL rule forbids shipping, and it was found by accident while chasing an a11y note about corner curvature rather than by any gate. It is now fixed via component/dropdown/border/radius-default, but the remaining non-colour surface is still unaudited, so there may be more of the same. Note the variable audit is not a substitute: it verified the tokens' own alias chains carry no INTERNAL, which was true, while the canvas binding was the thing at fault. A sweep needs to walk nodes and check every boundVariables field, not just the paint ones. Max chose to add the token and close out rather than sweep first, so this is a deliberate deferral, not an oversight.
_openQuestions.missing-hover-border-token: OPEN, logged 2026-08-08. Scania hovers an option by changing the bottom BORDER, not the background, and nothing in this spec carries that value. Scania core: `--tds-dropdown-option-border-hover` resolves grey-850 Light / grey-50 Dark, against an at-rest `--tds-dropdown-option-border` of grey-200 / grey-600, and the hover rule sets no background at all. The Tegel UI Library agrees byte for byte — a full layer walk of the hover variants (the option has only two layers, root plus label, so there is nowhere else to look) shows the root stroke moving grey/200 to grey/850 in Light and grey/600 to grey/50 in Dark, with the fill unchanged. Proposed token: component/dropdown/border/item/divider-hover, pairing with the existing border/item/divider-default. SECOND, RELATED FINDING: background/item/*/hover resolves Scania-Light to grey/100 (#EDEFF3), a colour neither Scania source paints for this component — so those Scania values look invented rather than observed. This is a cross-brand PATTERN divergence, not a value one: tegel-lite does paint a hover background, so TRATON hovers with fill while Scania hovers with border. Deciding it means choosing whether the brands keep different hover patterns or converge. Full evidence in tokens/audit/20260806-dropdown-variant-reduction/variant-matrix-11a.md, finding F11.
